title: Point-contact transistor demonstrated
before: Vacuum tubes amplified and switched signals but were bulky, hot, and relatively fragile for dense computing.
problem: Electronics needed smaller, more reliable switching elements to scale computing hardware.
change: Bell Labs researchers demonstrated the point-contact transistor in 1947 (widely documented in computing history timelines and semiconductor histories such as the Computer History Museum's Silicon Engine).
whyItMattered: Solid-state switching made miniaturization and energy efficiency practical over the following decades.
enabled: Transistor radios, then transistorized computers, then integrated circuits.
concreteExample: A phone SoC packing billions of transistors would be impossible with vacuum-tube switches.
caveat: Commercial and junction-transistor developments continued after 1947; the date marks a pivotal demonstration, not the end of the story.
